## Service Overview

RED signals per service. Mirrors the Splunk `Service Overview` dashboard tab.

Request data comes from the App Insights `requests` table, which the `azure_monitor` exporter populates from SERVER and CONSUMER spans.

content.query:
requests
| summarize Requests = sum(itemCount), Errors = sumif(itemCount, tobool(success) == false)
    by Service = cloud_RoleName
| extend ['Error rate %'] = iff(Requests == 0, 0.0, round(100.0 * Errors / Requests, 2))
| order by Requests desc
content.title: Requests and error rate by service

content.query:
let bin_ = {TimeRange:grain};
requests
| where cloud_RoleName == 'rag-api'
| summarize Requests = sum(itemCount) by bin(timestamp, bin_)
| project timestamp, ['Requests/s'] = todouble(Requests) / (bin_ / 1s)
| order by timestamp asc
content.title: Request rate (rag-api)

content.query:
let bin_ = {TimeRange:grain};
requests
| where cloud_RoleName == 'rag-api'
| summarize P50 = percentile(duration, 50),
            P90 = percentile(duration, 90),
            P99 = percentile(duration, 99)
    by bin(timestamp, bin_)
| order by timestamp asc
content.title: Service latency P50 / P90 / P99 (ms)

content.query:
requests
| where cloud_RoleName == 'rag-api' and tobool(success) == false
| summarize Errors = sum(itemCount) by Endpoint = name
| top 5 by Errors desc
content.title: Error count by endpoint (top 5)

content.query:
requests
| where cloud_RoleName == 'rag-api'
| summarize Requests = sum(itemCount) by Endpoint = name
| top 10 by Requests desc
content.title: Top endpoints (top 10)

content.json: > The `/health` endpoint is not filtered out of the two tables above, matching the Splunk charts exactly. Docker's healthcheck plus the Nginx upstream probe will dominate `Top endpoints` as a result.

## RAG Pipeline

Per-step latency through the retrieval and ingestion pipelines.

Every span on this tab is CLIENT or INTERNAL, so all of it lands in the `dependencies` table with its native per-span `duration`. **No spanmetrics connector is involved.** Splunk needs one because its MetricSets cover only SERVER and CONSUMER spans; App Insights has no such gap. See `docs/splunk-vs-azure-monitor.md`.

> **Active sessions counts only real sessions.** `session.id` is stamped on the HTTP SERVER span by the http instrumentation's `startIncomingSpanHook`, and is never invented when a client sends no `X-Session-Id` header. It previously came from Express middleware via `trace.getActiveSpan()`, which returns the middleware's own INTERNAL span, so it never reached `requests` at all and this tile read 0. Fixed in `api/src/session-attributes.js`.

content.query:
let bin_ = {TimeRange:grain};
dependencies
| where cloud_RoleName == 'rag-api'
| extend genai_op = tostring(customDimensions['gen_ai.operation.name'])
| extend Step = case(
    name startswith 'invoke_agent', 'Total Chat',
    name == 'db.vectorSearch',                         'Vector Search',
    genai_op == 'chat',                                'LLM Completion',
    genai_op == 'embeddings',                          'Query Embedding',
    '')
| where Step != ''
| summarize P50 = percentile(duration, 50) by bin(timestamp, bin_), Step
| order by timestamp asc
content.title: RAG chat pipeline latency, P50 by step (ms)

content.query:
let bin_ = {TimeRange:grain};
dependencies
| where cloud_RoleName == 'rag-api'
| extend genai_op = tostring(customDimensions['gen_ai.operation.name'])
| extend Step = case(
    name == 'upload.pipeline', 'Total Upload',
    genai_op == 'embeddings',  'Embedding',
    name == 'db.insertChunks', 'DB Insert',
    '')
| where Step != ''
| summarize P50 = percentile(duration, 50) by bin(timestamp, bin_), Step
| order by timestamp asc
content.title: RAG upload pipeline latency, P50 by step (ms)

    cloud_RoleName == 'playwright-mcp' and name == 'mcp.tool.browser_navigate', 'Navigate',
    cloud_RoleName == 'playwright-mcp' and name == 'mcp.tool.browser_get_text', 'Get Text',

| where cloud_RoleName == 'rag-api'
| extend SessionId = tostring(customDimensions['session.id'])
| where isnotempty(SessionId)
| summarize ['Active sessions'] = dcount(SessionId)
content.title: Active sessions

## LLM and AI

Token economics, model attribution and inference latency, from `gen_ai.*` semantic-convention attributes.

Token totals read the `gen_ai.client.token.count` counter in `customMetrics`. That is only correct because the counter arrives with **delta** temporality (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_TEMPORALITY_PREFERENCE=delta` in `docker-compose.yml`). Under cumulative temporality `sum(valueSum)` would sum a monotonic ramp.

Response length percentiles read the **span attribute**, not the histogram metric: the `azure_monitor` exporter flattens histogram buckets, so a true P90 cannot be recovered from `customMetrics`.

content.query:
customMetrics
| where name == 'gen_ai.client.token.count' and cloud_RoleName == 'rag-api'
| summarize Tokens = tolong(sum(valueSum))
    by ['Token type'] = tostring(customDimensions['gen_ai.token.type'])
| order by ['Token type'] asc
content.title: Total tokens by type

content.query:
dependencies
| where cloud_RoleName == 'rag-api'
| where tostring(customDimensions['gen_ai.operation.name']) == 'chat'
| summarize Calls = sum(itemCount),
            ['P50 ms']        = round(percentile(duration, 50), 0),
            ['Input tokens']  = sum(tolong(tostring(customDimensions['gen_ai.usage.input_tokens']))),
            ['Output tokens'] = sum(tolong(tostring(customDimensions['gen_ai.usage.output_tokens'])))
    by Provider          = tostring(customDimensions['gen_ai.provider.name']),
       ['Request model']  = tostring(customDimensions['gen_ai.request.model']),
       ['Response model'] = tostring(customDimensions['gen_ai.response.model'])
| order by Calls desc
content.title: LLM provider and model

content.query:
dependencies
| where cloud_RoleName == 'rag-api'
| where tostring(customDimensions['gen_ai.operation.name']) == 'embeddings'
| summarize Calls = sum(itemCount),
            ['P50 ms']       = round(percentile(duration, 50), 0),
            ['Input tokens'] = sum(tolong(tostring(customDimensions['gen_ai.usage.input_tokens'])))
    by Provider   = tostring(customDimensions['gen_ai.provider.name']),
       Model      = tostring(customDimensions['gen_ai.request.model']),
       Dimensions = tostring(customDimensions['gen_ai.response.dimensions'])
| order by Calls desc
content.title: Embedding model

## Infrastructure

Container and SurrealDB resource metrics, from the collector's `docker_stats` receiver and SurrealDB's own OTLP export.

> **These charts reach parity; the product around them does not.** Application Insights has no infrastructure experience. Splunk's Infrastructure Navigators and APM-to-Infrastructure Related Content, keyed on `host.name`, have no App Insights counterpart, so `resourcedetection` buys nothing here. Azure's equivalents (VM Insights, Container Insights) run off the Azure Monitor Agent against a Log Analytics workspace, not off custom metrics. See `docs/splunk-vs-azure-monitor.md`.

The counters below are delta-converted by `cumulativetodelta` in the collector. Without that they would render as monotonic ramps, because `customMetrics` has no counter semantics.

content.query:
let bin_ = {TimeRange:grain};
customMetrics
| where name == 'container.cpu.usage.total'
| extend Container = coalesce(tostring(customDimensions['compose.service']),
                              tostring(customDimensions['container.name']))
| summarize CpuNs = sum(valueSum) by bin(timestamp, bin_), Container
| project timestamp, Container, ['CPU cores'] = round(todouble(CpuNs) / 1e9 / (bin_ / 1s), 3)
| order by timestamp asc
content.title: Container CPU usage (cores)

content.query:
let bin_ = {TimeRange:grain};
customMetrics
| where name == 'container.memory.usage.total'
| extend Container = coalesce(tostring(customDimensions['compose.service']),
                              tostring(customDimensions['container.name']))
| summarize ['Memory MiB'] = round(avg(valueSum) / 1048576.0, 1)
    by bin(timestamp, bin_), Container
| order by timestamp asc
content.title: Container memory usage (MiB)

content.query:
let bin_ = {TimeRange:grain};
customMetrics
| where name in ('container.network.io.usage.rx_bytes', 'container.network.io.usage.tx_bytes')
| extend Direction = iff(name endswith 'rx_bytes', 'Received bytes/s', 'Sent bytes/s')
| summarize Bytes = sum(valueSum) by bin(timestamp, bin_), Direction
| project timestamp, Direction, ['Bytes/s'] = round(todouble(Bytes) / (bin_ / 1s), 1)
| order by timestamp asc
content.title: Container network I/O

content.query:

| where cloud_RoleName == 'surrealdb' and name == 'surrealdb.process.cpu_percent'
| summarize ['CPU %'] = round(avg(valueSum), 2) by bin(timestamp, bin_)
| order by timestamp asc
content.title: SurrealDB process CPU (%)

content.json:
## Logs and Traces

**This tab has no Splunk equivalent in this project, and that is the point.**

Application logs land in the App Insights `traces` table in the same resource as the spans, correlated by `operation_Id`, with no extra configuration and no second product. On the Splunk side logs go to Splunk Cloud Platform via HEC, and the single-pane correlation view (Log Observer Connect) is blocked on a non-trial licence -- see `docs/splunk-setup.md` Section 26.

DEBUG and TRACE records are dropped by the collector's `filter/logs` processor before egress, so only INFO and above appear here.

content.query:
let bin_ = {TimeRange:grain};
traces
| extend Severity = case(severityLevel == 0, 'VERBOSE',
                         severityLevel == 1, 'INFO',
                         severityLevel == 2, 'WARN',
                         severityLevel == 3, 'ERROR',
                         severityLevel == 4, 'CRITICAL',
                         'UNKNOWN')
| summarize Records = count() by bin(timestamp, bin_), Severity
| order by timestamp asc
content.title: Log volume by severity

content.query:
exceptions
| summarize Count = sum(itemCount), ['Last seen'] = max(timestamp)
    by Type = type, Method = outerMethod
| top 20 by Count desc
content.title: Exceptions by type

content.query:
traces
| where severityLevel >= 3
| project timestamp, Service = cloud_RoleName, Message = message,
          Operation = operation_Name, ['Trace ID'] = operation_Id
| order by timestamp desc
| take 100
content.title: Recent errors (click a Trace ID to correlate with its spans)
